newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Hero profit eases on restructuring charges.
newsitem.headline: Hero profit eases on restructuring charges.

text.p: Swiss food and beverage maker Hero AG said 1996 group net profit eased to 31.9 million Swiss francs from 35.6 million, mainly due to extraordinary restructuring charges of more than 20 million.

Hero, majority-owned by German foods group Schwartau International GmbH., also said 1996 pre-tax profit rose to 56.9 million from 46.2 million, helped by currency gains and the divestments of activities.
The net result includes a 34 percent rise in depreciation to 90 million francs, mainly due to the first-time consolidation of previous Schwartau companies and goodwill write offs.
Operating profit rose 26.4 percent to 88.5 million francs, but Hero said in statement that an operating margin of 4.8 percent was not at all in line with management's targets.
"Based on measures already taken, a significant improvement can be expected already in the current year," Hero said.
Hero added that it expected an acceleration of the positive development seen since the second half of 1996.
The company's management proposes an unchanged dividend of 19 francs per bearer share and 4.75 franc per registered share.
Hero's group sales last year rose 27.9 percent to 1.84 billion and cash flow rose 19 percent to 121.9 million.
Combined with sales of participations and a reduction in working capital, Hero also expects to significantly reduce its debt in 1997.
